evidence_sources.claim_summary: Aave v2 protocol repository commit "TheGraph: major update to the latest deployed subgraph, codegen fixes", the last public commit on the archived repository; it dates the end of public engineering activity on this codebase.
Current official documentation portal for Aave; documents v3 as the active market and does not describe v2 control-plane procedures.
Aave's published security review index, listing the audits that cover the v2 deployment period.

Earliest archived copy of Aave's developer documentation in the period preceding the v2 provider configuration (2020-11-30), establishing that public control-plane documentation existed before the deployment it describes.

The documentation portal moved to aave.com/docs by 2024-10-26 and documents v3; the archived v2 developer site is no longer served, which is the documentation gap this dossier records rather than an assumption.

gap_windows.summary: The provider was configured across 21 calls in a 3-day window; after the last call on 2020-12-03 no further provider-level mutation is recorded, so the control plane has been static for the remainder of the dossier window.

executive_risk_memo: Aave v2's control plane is the PoolAddressesProvider at 0xB53C1a33016B2DC2fF3653530bfF1848a515c8c5, and every provider-level mutation it has ever executed sits inside a three-day window at the end of 2020: twelve pool-admin rotations, the lending-pool and configurator implementation writes, both oracle writes, two emergency-admin writes and a final ownership transfer on 2020-12-03. Since then the provider has been called thousands of times, but those calls are user-facing methods such as flashLoan and deposit, not governance. The consequence for due diligence is that a borrower's exposure to Aave v2 today depends on a control plane nobody has touched in roughly six years, which is stability of a specific kind: the absence of recent operational exercise on the one path that could still change the implementation. Engineering bench strength cannot be measured from the repository because aave/aave-protocol was archived in 2024, showing zero commits in the trailing twelve months and no human contributors, so bus factor is reported as zero rather than inferred. Public documentation has moved to Aave v3 entirely, meaning a verifier working from current docs cannot reconstruct v2 control-plane procedure without the archived repository and on-chain history. The honest reading is a mature, frozen protocol whose risk is concentrated in the lack of recent practice on its upgrade path rather than in governance churn. Two selectors that Blockscout leaves undecoded were resolved before counting: 0xab9c4b5d is flashLoan and 0xe8eda9df is deposit, and the only selector 4byte.directory still reports as unknown, 0x86f3a74f, is requestFlashLoan(uint256,address) per openchain.xyz. So every one of the 38 provider calls after 2020 is a user-facing method, and none of them is governance. The TVL figure in this file is the protocol total reported by DefiLlama at dossier time (83,574,773 USD); the Ethereum deployment this dossier audits is the largest single chain at roughly 64.2M USD of that total, and the two numbers are stated separately so a reviewer recomputing from the same page sees no discrepancy.
